source: Goh et al. (2024) Large language model influence on diagnostic reasoning: a randomized clinical trial
finding: Giving 50 physicians GPT-4 (ChatGPT Plus) did not raise their diagnostic reasoning score over conventional resources.
numbers: Single-blind RCT, Nov 29-Dec 29 2023. 50 physicians (26 attending, 24 resident), 25 per arm. 244 cases (125 LLM, 119 control). Median score 76% (IQR 66-87) LLM vs 74% (IQR 63-84) control; adjusted diff 2 points (95% CI -4 to 8; P=.60). 6 landmark vignettes, 60 minutes.
quote: the availability of an LLM to physicians as a diagnostic aid did not significantly improve clinical reasoning
limits: Small sample, one commercial LLM, one zero-shot prompt, no training in prompting, vignettes not live patients. Power was set to detect 8 points.
agent_relevance: Access to a strong model is not enough. How the human or the loop uses the model decides the gain.

source: Goh et al. (2024) Large language model influence on diagnostic reasoning: a randomized clinical trial (LLM alone arm)
finding: GPT-4 alone, run 3 times with a plain zero-shot prompt, beat both physician groups on the same rubric.
numbers: LLM alone median 92% (IQR 82-97) per case; 16 points above the conventional-resources group (95% CI 2-30; P=.03). Physicians+LLM 76%.
limits: Exploratory secondary analysis. Three runs nested under one 'participant'. Graders blinded; weighted kappa 0.66, Cronbach alpha 0.64.
agent_relevance: Large gap between model alone (92) and human with model (76): the human step lost value. Our agent should not pass control to a free-form step that discards the model's own differential.

source: Goh et al. (2024) Large language model influence on diagnostic reasoning: a randomized clinical trial (secondary outcomes, subgroups)
finding: No benefit in any subgroup; time saving not significant; final-diagnosis odds only weakly higher.
numbers: Attendings +0.5 points (P=.92); residents +3 (CI -6 to 11; P=.50); LLM use under monthly -0.5 (P=.90); over monthly +5 (CI -7 to 16; P=.40). Time per case 519 s vs 565 s (diff -82 s; CI -195 to 31). Final dx ordinal OR 1.4 (CI 0.7-2.8), binary OR 1.9 (CI 0.9-4.0; P=.10). 22 of 22 readable LLM transcripts showed LLM use.
limits: Subgroups underpowered. 3 transcripts lost. Authors suggest prompt training, predefined prompts, or an LLM that points out features that do not fit the differential.
agent_relevance: Authors' own fix idea (point out non-fitting features) matches a counter-evidence operator in our schema.

source: Goh et al. (2024) Large language model influence on diagnostic reasoning: a randomized clinical trial (rubric design)
finding: Primary outcome was a structured-reflection rubric, not only final accuracy: top-3 differential, findings for and against each, final diagnosis, next steps.
numbers: Points: 1 per plausible diagnosis; 0/1/2 for supporting and opposing findings; final dx 0-2; up to 3 next steps at 0/1/2. Cases adapted from a landmark 105-case computer-diagnosis study (never public). Power: over 80% to detect 8 points, SD 16.2%, ICC 0.05-0.15.
limits: Rubric alpha only 0.64. Scoring partly subjective.
agent_relevance: A graded reasoning trace has for/against evidence per hypothesis. Template for our hypothesis table state.

source: Kanjee, Crowe, Rodman (2023) Accuracy of a generative AI model in a complex diagnostic challenge (JAMA)
finding: GPT-4 on 70 NEJM clinicopathological conference cases put the final diagnosis in its differential 64% of the time.
numbers: 70 cases analysed (80 found, 10 excluded). Final dx in differential 64% (45/70); top diagnosis correct 39% (27/70); mean differential length 9.0; mean rank of correct dx 2.5; quality score median 5; scorer agreement 66%, kappa 0.57.
limits: Some case data left out of prompts; puzzles, not routine care; moderate rater agreement; black box.
agent_relevance: Baseline for the field: single prompt, no scaffold, 39% top-1. Later studies move from here.

source: McDuff et al. (2023/2025) Towards accurate differential diagnosis with large language models
finding: A PaLM-2-based LLM tuned for differentials beat unassisted clinicians on 302 NEJM CPC cases, and helped clinicians as an aid.
numbers: Standalone top-10 59.1% vs 33.6% unassisted clinicians (p=0.04); standalone top-1 29.2%. Assisted: LLM arm top-10 51.8% vs search arm 44.5% (abstract: 51.7% vs 44.4% and 36.1% without help; McNemar 45.7, p<0.01 vs no help; 4.75, p=0.03 vs search). 20 clinicians, each case read by 2, randomized to search or LLM+search; unaided list written first.
limits: Generalists, not specialists; text only; CPC puzzles; clinicians told not to ask about unreported labs.
agent_relevance: Within-person design (unaided list first, then aided) is a clean test. The LLM mostly added breadth to the list, which fits a 'widen the differential' operator.

source: McDuff et al. (2023/2025) Towards accurate differential diagnosis with large language models (Table 1 and overlap set)
finding: Table 1 splits top-1 and top-10 by condition; assistance helped the list more than the top pick.
numbers: Full set (302): LLM 29.2/59.1 (top-1/top-10); clinicians before help 15.9/33.6; after search 24.3/44.5; after LLM 25.2/51.8. No-overlap set (56 cases): LLM 35.4/55.4; before 13.8/34.6; search 29.2/46.2; LLM 24.6/52.3. On the 70-case GPT-4 set the tuned LLM did better for top-N when N is above 2.
limits: Different raters than the GPT-4 study, so top-10 is compared only through an automated metric. Contamination analysis on pretraining data was run (details not read).
agent_relevance: List breadth is cheap to gain; the top-1 rank is hard to move.

source: Tu et al. (2024) Towards conversational diagnostic AI (AMIE)
finding: AMIE, an LLM tuned with self-play, beat 20 primary care physicians on differential accuracy in text OSCE consultations.
numbers: 149 scenarios (Canada, UK, India), 20 PCPs, 20 patient actors, randomized double-blind crossover. Superior on 28 of 32 specialist axes and 24 of 26 patient-actor axes; top-k accuracy higher at all k (permutation n=10,000, FDR-corrected p<0.05). Mean 149.8 turns per conversation.
limits: Text chat unfamiliar to PCPs; simulated patients; not real care. Authors say not representative of practice.
agent_relevance: Self-play with an inner critic loop is a loop method already used on this subfield.

source: Tu et al. (2024) Towards conversational diagnostic AI (AMIE) (information gathering)
finding: Top-3 differential accuracy plateaued within about 10 turns for both AMIE and PCPs, so AMIE did not gather information faster.
numbers: Truncated-conversation analysis with AMIE producing the differentials: plateau in first 10 turns for both. AMIE wrote more words but elicited a similar number of patient words.
limits: Auto-evaluation used AMIE itself to produce the truncated differentials.
agent_relevance: The edge came from reasoning over the same information, not from asking better questions.

source: Tu et al. (2024) Towards conversational diagnostic AI (AMIE) (inner and outer self-play)
finding: Training loop: inner self-play with an in-context critic refines dialogues with an AI patient; outer loop fine-tunes on retained dialogues.
numbers: Design: AI patient, AI critic, inner loop refinement, outer loop on retained dialogues, auto-evaluation of reasoning chain and honesty.
limits: Critic is an LLM; no independent check beyond the scenario's ground truth.
agent_relevance: A concrete critic inside a loop; ours should be code-checked rather than model-judged (G5).

source: Brodeur et al. (2024) Superhuman performance of a large language model on the reasoning tasks of a physician
finding: OpenAI o1-preview put the correct diagnosis in its differential in 78.3% of 143 NEJM CPC cases.
numbers: 78.3% (95% CI 70.7-84.8); first diagnosis correct 52% (CI 44-61). Before vs after training cutoff 79.8% vs 73.5% (p=0.59). On 70 cases used for GPT-4: 88.6% vs 72.9% (p=.015). Rater agreement 120/143, kappa 0.66. Correct test chosen 87.5%, helpful another 11%.
limits: Model only; no human-LLM interaction; CPC puzzles; the cutoff split shows no clear contamination effect but is small.
agent_relevance: Reasoning models raised the single-prompt baseline by about 15 points. Model strength is a confound for any scaffold gain.

source: Brodeur et al. (2024) Superhuman performance of a large language model on the reasoning tasks of a physician (NEJM Healer and management cases)
finding: o1-preview documented reasoning at near-perfect R-IDEA level and far above physicians on management cases.
numbers: R-IDEA perfect in 78/80 vs GPT-4 47/80, attendings 28/80, residents 16/80 (all p<0.0001). Grey Matters management: o1 median 86% vs GPT-4 42%, physicians+GPT-4 41%, physicians conventional 34%; o1 +41.6 points over GPT-4 (CI 22.9-60.4). Cannot-miss diagnoses at triage median 0.92 (not significantly different).
limits: Historical controls from earlier studies; different raters; only 5 management vignettes.
agent_relevance: Physicians with GPT-4 (41%) did no better than GPT-4 alone (42%) on management here, echoing Goh 2024.

source: Brodeur et al. (2024) Superhuman performance of a large language model on the reasoning tasks of a physician (landmark cases and ER second opinions)
finding: o1 scored 97% on the same 6 landmark cases where physicians with GPT-4 scored 76%; in a real ER study o1 beat two attendings at each touchpoint.
numbers: Landmark: o1 97% vs GPT-4 92%, physicians+GPT-4 76%, physicians conventional 74%; o1 vs conventional +20.2 points (CI -0.4 to 40.9; p=0.055). ER, 79 cases: exact or very close dx at triage 65.8%, physician 69.6%, admission 79.7% for o1 vs attending 1: 54.4/60.8/75.9 and attending 2: 48.1/50.6/68.4. Raters could not tell source about 84% of the time.
limits: ER arm is proof of concept: second-opinion task, two attendings, record data, not live. Probabilistic reasoning: o1 similar to GPT-4 except one case.
agent_relevance: Gap was largest at triage, where information is least: scaffolds that widen early hypotheses pay most there.

source: Bean et al. (2025) Clinical knowledge in LLMs does not translate to human interactions
finding: Members of the public with an LLM did no better than a control group at naming conditions or disposition, though the same LLMs alone were accurate.
numbers: 1,298 UK participants, 10 scenarios. LLMs alone: conditions 94.9%, disposition 56.3%. With participants: conditions under 34.5%, disposition under 44.2%; control found at least one condition in 47.0%. LLM suggested a relevant condition in at least 65.7% of conversations.
quote: user interactions as a challenge to the deployment of LLMs for medical advice
limits: Lay users not clinicians; GPT-4o, Llama 3, Command R+; text only; 10 scenarios.
agent_relevance: Failures came from the interface: incomplete input, misread prompts, advice not followed. Our agent must elicit full inputs itself.

source: Bean et al. (2025) Clinical knowledge in LLMs does not translate to human interactions (benchmarks and simulated users)
finding: Licensing-style question accuracy did not predict interactive results, and LLM-simulated users did not stand in for real ones.
numbers: Question-answer score higher than interactive score in 26 of 30 model-scenario pairs and largely uncorrelated with it. Simulated participants did better than humans, had less variance, and correlated only weakly.
limits: Simulation method adapted from patient-simulation work; one design.
agent_relevance: Do not trust a self-simulated user or an exam score as the test of the loop; test on held-out real output (G3).

source: Nori et al. (2025) Sequential diagnosis with language models (SDBench, MAI-DxO)
finding: A benchmark of 304 NEJM CPC cases turned into step-by-step encounters; physicians scored 20%, off-the-shelf o3 78.6%.
numbers: Physicians (generalists, median 12 years): 19.9% at $2,963 per case, 11.8 min, 6.6 questions, 7.2 tests, 764 diagnoses over 56 test cases. GPT-4o 49.3% at $2,745; o3 78.6% at $7,850. Best single physician 41%.
limits: Physicians barred from search, books and colleagues; CPC cases have no healthy or benign patients; gatekeeper is an o4-mini model with synthetic findings (508 responses reviewed); US cost estimates.
agent_relevance: The 20% physician figure comes from a restricted setting. Do not read it as general physician skill.

source: Nori et al. (2025) Sequential diagnosis with language models (SDBench, MAI-DxO) (MAI-DxO orchestrator)
finding: A scaffold of five role-played 'doctors' raised o3 from 78.6% to 81.9% and cut cost from $7,850 to $4,735.
numbers: Panel: Dr. Hypothesis (probability-ranked top 3, Bayesian updates), Dr. Test-Chooser (up to 3 tests), Dr. Challenger (devil's advocate, anchoring check), Dr. Stewardship (cost), Dr. Checklist (validity). Budgeted variant 79.9% at $2,396; ensemble 85.5% at $7,184; baseline o3 78.6%. Gains significant for all other models (p<0.005, paired permutation, 10,000 resamples), larger for weaker models.
limits: Same-model personas share errors (our G4); no healthy cases, no false-positive rate; mainly developed on GPT-4.1. No per-role ablation in the text read.
agent_relevance: Precedent for a hypothesis table, a falsifier role and a stop threshold inside an LLM loop. It uses persona agents, which our G4 warns are not independent.

source: Nori et al. (2025) Sequential diagnosis with language models (SDBench, MAI-DxO) (anchoring in the baseline)
finding: Off-the-shelf o3 anchored on its first impression and ordered tests that were 'reasonable' rather than informative; MAI-DxO sought disconfirming evidence.
numbers: Example: alcohol withdrawal patient who drank hand sanitizer. Baseline o3 fixated on antibiotic toxicity, ordered MRI and EEG, wrong, $3,431. MAI-DxO asked about in-hospital toxins first, correct, $795.
limits: One case picked in a manual review of disagreements.
agent_relevance: Supports a forced-alternatives step before ordering tests, tied to a signal such as a failed check (G1), not a schedule.

source: Savage et al. (2023/2024) Diagnostic reasoning prompts reveal the potential for LLM interpretability in medicine
finding: Prompting GPT-4 to reason like a clinician (differential, analytic, Bayesian, intuitive) kept accuracy level with plain chain of thought; GPT-3.5 got worse.
numbers: MedQA free-response. GPT-3.5: CoT 46%; intuitive 48% (P=0.9); analytic 40% (-6, P=0.001); differential diagnosis 38% (-8, P<0.001); Bayesian 42% (-4, P=0.02). GPT-4: CoT 76%; intuitive 77% (P=0.73); differential 78% (P=0.24); analytic 78% (P=0.35); Bayesian 72% (-3.4, P=0.07). Rater agreement 97-99%.
limits: Exam questions, not patients; prompts not exhaustive; rationale quality and hallucination not checked.
agent_relevance: Clinical-style prompts buy interpretability, not accuracy. A weak model can be hurt by imposed structure.

source: Hager et al. (2024) Evaluation and mitigation of the limitations of LLMs in clinical decision-making (Nature Medicine)
finding: On 2,400 real MIMIC-IV patients with four abdominal diagnoses, open LLMs diagnosed worse than doctors and broke instructions.
numbers: Full-information accuracy 58.8% (Llama 2 Chat), 67.8% (OASST), 65.1% (WizardLM); autonomous information gathering lowered these to 45.5%, 54.9%, 53.9%. Models 16-25 points below physicians on an 80-patient subset (German residents 87.5%, US hospitalist 92.5%; P<0.001). Action errors every 2-4 patients; hallucinated tools every 2-5.
limits: Open 2023-era models, not GPT-4 or reasoning models; per-pathology numbers only in figures; no chain-of-thought ablation; page read to about 100k of 127k characters.
agent_relevance: Dated, but lists failure modes a loop must guard: format errors, invented tools, lab misreading.

source: Hager et al. (2024) (order and quantity of information)
finding: Changing the order of the same evidence changed accuracy, and giving fewer exams sometimes helped.
numbers: Order shifts up to 18.0 points (Chat, pancreatitis), 7.9 (OASST), 5.4 (WizardLM). Radiologist reports only raised cholecystitis by 18.5 (Chat); labs only raised pancreatitis by 21.6. Lab interpretation of low values correct: 26.5% / 70.2% / 45.8%.
limits: As in the previous line.
agent_relevance: Support for order-invariance checks and for mutated inputs as a test (G3).

source: Goh et al. (2025) GPT-4 assistance for improvement of physician performance on patient care tasks (Nature Medicine)
finding: A second RCT, on management reasoning, found a real gain for physicians with GPT-4.
numbers: 92 physicians, Nov 2023-Apr 2024, 5 expert vignettes, GPT-4 plus conventional vs conventional only. Total score +6.5% (95% CI 2.7-10.2; P<0.001). Time +119.3 s per case (CI 17.4-221.2; P=0.02). Physicians+LLM vs LLM alone -0.9% (CI -9.0 to 7.2; P=0.8). NCT06208423.
limits: Read from the abstract record only (Europe PMC, PMC12380382), not the full text. Management, not diagnosis; simulated vignettes.
agent_relevance: Task type matters: management gained, diagnosis did not (Goh 2024). Here the human plus model did not exceed the model alone.

source: Qiu et al. (2025) Quantifying the reasoning abilities of LLMs on real-world clinical cases (MedR-Bench)
finding: On 1,453 structured case reports, reasoning LLMs reached 89.8% diagnosis with all key results given but less when they had to gather them.
numbers: DeepSeek-R1 diagnostic accuracy 71.79% (1-turn), 76.18% (free-turn), 89.76% (oracle). o3-mini 64.99% to 67.19% free-turn. Gemini-2.0-FT 68.55% 1-turn. Exam-recommendation recall best 43.61% (R1). Reasoning factuality over 90% but key steps missed. 656 rare-disease cases.
limits: Cases rewritten by GPT-4o; automated reasoning evaluator; Baichuan-M1 fell in free-turn.
agent_relevance: The bottleneck is choosing what to ask for, not reading results. Information seeking is where a scaffold should help.

source: Saab et al. (2024) Capabilities of Gemini models in medicine (Med-Gemini)
finding: Self-training with search plus uncertainty-guided search at inference raised MedQA to 91.1% and NEJM CPC top-10 by 4.0 points.
numbers: MedQA: self-training +3.2 points; search rounds lift 87.2% to 91.1%. NEJM CPC (303 cases): +4.0 points top-10 with one search iteration; a table row lists 72.3 vs 59.1 (McDuff) and 50.0 for top-10.
limits: Search is triggered by model uncertainty; benchmark, not a human trial; web pages may be contaminated.
agent_relevance: A named loop element: uncertainty-gated retrieval. The gate matches 'doubt only on a signal' (G1).

source: Palepu et al. (2025) Towards conversational AI for disease management (AMIE)
finding: AMIE with guideline retrieval and structured reasoning matched primary care physicians on management reasoning.
numbers: Randomized blinded virtual OSCE: 100 multi-visit scenarios, 21 PCPs. AMIE non-inferior on management per specialists; better on precision of treatments and investigations and on guideline grounding. RxQA drug benchmark: AMIE beat PCPs on higher-difficulty items.
limits: Simulated patients; UK guidelines (NICE, BMJ Best Practice); only abstract and introduction read.
agent_relevance: In-context guideline retrieval is a grounding step that checks claims against a document.

source: Nori et al. (2023) Capabilities of GPT-4 on medical challenge problems
finding: GPT-4 with no medical tuning passed USMLE by wide margins and was better calibrated than earlier models.
numbers: USMLE average 86.65% and 86.7% (two official test sets); abstract also reports calibration and memorization tests.
limits: Multiple-choice exams; lower table columns (83.76, 53.61, 49.10) were not matched to model names.
agent_relevance: Exam scores saturate and predict little about interactive use (see Bean 2025).

source: Semigran et al. (2015) Evaluation of symptom checkers for self diagnosis and triage (BMJ)
finding: Pre-LLM systems for the same task: online symptom checkers listed the right diagnosis first in about a third of vignettes.
numbers: From memory, unverified: 23 checkers, 45 vignettes; correct first about 34%, within 20 about 58%, physicians far higher.
limits: Not opened this session; numbers may be off.
agent_relevance: Pre-LLM baseline; verify before citing.

source: Brodeur et al. (2024) introduction on Ledley and Lusted (1959) and CPC benchmarks
finding: Case-based diagnostic benchmarks (NEJM CPC series) have been the test of differential generators since the 1950s, from Bayesian and rule-based systems to symptom checkers.
numbers: No numbers for the early systems in the text read.
limits: Secondary description only; Ledley and Lusted not opened.
agent_relevance: CPC cases are the standard and so a likely contamination source.
